title: Righteous God! Whose Vengeful Phials
description: Righteous God! Whose Vengeful Phials in Tonic Solfa to RUSTINGTON, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 60.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7.8.7.8.7), and this page sets them to RUSTINGTON; any other Eights and Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Right-eous God! whose venge-ful phi-als All our fears and thoughts ex-ceed, Big with woes and fie-ry tri-als, Hang-ing, burst-ing o'er our head; While thou vis-i-test the na-tions, Thy se-lect-ed peo-ple spare; Arm our cau-tioned souls with pa-tience, Fill our hum-bled hearts with prayer.

lines: All our fears and thoughts exceed,
Big with woes and fiery trials,
Arm our cautioned souls with patience,
Fill our humbled hearts with prayer.
With all flesh is now begun,
Mercy first and last be shown;
Plead thy cause with sword and fire,
Shake us till the curse remove,
Till thou com'st, the world's desire,
From this ruined earth and skies,
Vanish, then, this world of shadows,
Lord, appear! appear to glad us
With the dawn of endless day
Now descend, and take thy bride!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to RUSTINGTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
